### Observed differences

- Before, each of A14, A18, A21, A22 and A23 (each present in about 16–23% of traces; together roughly one of them per case) sent all of its observed outgoing transitions to A24; in the later window, all of them send everything to A29 [DIR001, DIR005, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010].
- A15, A16, A17, A19 and A20 occur in every trace in both windows. Before, about 14–27% of each one's outgoing transitions went to A29 and none to A24; in the later window, about 17–25% go to A24 and none to A29, while routing among these five activities continues in both windows [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR006, DIR007].
- Before, A39 fed only A14/A18/A21/A22/A23 (shares of 16–23%, matching how often each occurs) and A28 fed only A15/A16/A17/A19/A20; in the later window, A39 feeds only A15/A16/A17/A19/A20 and A28 feeds only A14/A18/A21/A22/A23 [DIR011, DIR012].
- Event positions swapped accordingly: A14/A18/A21/A22/A23 moved from a mean position of about 0.32–0.33 to about 0.68–0.71 of the trace, A15/A16/A17/A19/A20 from about 0.62–0.63 to about 0.38–0.39, and A24 and A28 both shifted later by about 0.13 (0.36 to 0.48 and 0.54 to 0.66) while keeping their relative order [POS001, POS005, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS006, POS007, POS011, POS012].
- All 45 activity pairs spanning the two groups (or involving A24/A28) reversed their execution order; for example, A24 preceded A15 in 100% of traces before and 0% after, and A14 preceded A15 in about 21 in 100 co-occurrences before versus 0 after [REL001, REL012, REL013, REL026, REL040].
- Participation was stable: every involved activity keeps a substantial share of traces in both windows (A15–A20 in 100%, the others in about 16–23%), so no activity appeared, disappeared or changed in how often it runs [DIR001, DIR002, POS001, POS002].
- The elapsed time between consecutive completions from A30, A41 or A43 to A40 roughly halved, from about 1.0 hour before to about 0.5 hour in the later window (A30→A40: mean 1.01 to 0.49 h over 200 intervals; A41→A40: 1.01 to 0.52 h; A43→A40: 0.98 to 0.51 h) [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a re-sequencing in which the two five-activity groups exchanged their places around the A24–A28 segment: in the earlier window a case ran A39, then one of A14/A18/A21/A22/A23, then A24 and A28, then the group A15/A16/A17/A19/A20, which handed over to A29; in the later window the group order is reversed, with A39 leading into A15/A16/A17/A19/A20, which hand over to A24, and A28 leading into A14/A18/A21/A22/A23, which hand over to A29 [DIR011, DIR012, REL012, REL013, POS011, POS012].

This is shown directly and consistently: every one of the 45 cross-group order relations flips (several from complete precedence to complete reverse), the successor profiles of A39, A28 and the group exits rewire exactly as this re-sequencing implies, and the position shifts are large and symmetric; the 69 qualifying control-flow items and 3 time items far exceed the roughly 0.65 and 0.015 items expected without change, and each item's difference exceeds at least about 995 in 1,000 random re-splits; stable occurrence shares rule out activities being added, removed or made optional as the explanation [REL001, REL012, DIR011, DIR012, POS001, POS002, DIR001]. A competing explanation the two aggregate windows cannot fully exclude is a flip in the mix of two fixed process variants (from essentially only one order to essentially only the other), though the complete, symmetric reversals make a within-case re-sequencing the more direct reading; the many agreeing items also largely describe one underlying reordering rather than independent changes [REL001, REL012, DIR012].

Other differences: the elapsed time from the completions of A30, A41 or A43 to the following completion of A40 consistently fell from about 1.0 to about 0.5 hour — a timing change that stands as a hypothesis in its own right — and the evidence shows no link between it and the re-sequencing above [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, TWAIT003].

Now let me understand the behavioural story.

DIR items:
- DIR001 (A14): before, all outgoing transitions from A14 go to A24 (1.0); after, all go to A29 (1.0). Support 42 before, 33 after.

- DIR009 (A22): same. Support 41/39.
